notes: Unit conventions: the SEC filing presents financial statement line items in millions; all JSON currency outputs were converted to full USD units by multiplying by 1,000,000. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))

NWC definition used for this package: (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − current maturities of short-term borrowings). This matches the balance sheet structure and isolates operating working capital. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))

Tax rate: normalized effective tax rate estimate uses FY 2024–2025 income statement provision divided by pre-tax income; FY 2023 shows a tax benefit and was not used directly for the normalized rate. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))

NOL balance: interpreted from disclosed tax loss carryforwards available to offset future income ($3,016.5 million at Dec 31, 2025). NOL utilization percent is set to 1.00 (100%) as a modeling assumption consistent with management’s stated expectation of sufficient taxable income to recover remaining tax losses, but timing to exhaustion within the explicit forecast horizon is inherently uncertain. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))

WACC/terminal growth: treated as DCF modeling inputs (not explicitly disclosed in the extracted sources) and therefore should be stress-tested in a sensitivity table (base WACC 0.085; terminal growth 0.02).
Comparable multiples: EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, and P/E NTM were not populated from a primary/high-quality market-data source in this run, so comps contain nulls by design.

catalysts: Sustained delivery on 2026 sales growth and operating leverage guidance (transformation and productivity). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/77360/000007736026000003/a2025q4pressrelease.htm))
Any update from management on long-term outlook at upcoming investor communications (growth strategy and margin targets).

Capital allocation signals (dividend growth continuity and buyback pace) supported by free cash flow generation. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/77360/000007736026000003/a2025q4pressrelease.htm))
company_overview: Pentair plc is a global water-focused company serving customers across residential and commercial water solutions and pool-related applications.
Pentair reports operating income (GAAP) and generates substantial operating cash flow, funding dividends and capital expenditures.
Management describes a transformation-driven operating model (Pentair Business System) intended to expand returns on sales over time.
current_context: FY 2025 results: net sales of $4.2 billion (up 2% YoY) and operating income of $858 million (up 7% YoY). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))

Q4 2025 sales were $1.021 billion (up 5% YoY) with 2025 operating income of $858 million and FY free cash flow from continuing operations of $748 million. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/77360/000007736026000003/a2025q4pressrelease.htm))

2026 outlook (management): expects full-year 2026 sales up approximately 3% to 4% on a reported basis, alongside margin expansion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/77360/000007736026000003/a2025q4pressrelease.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue path anchors on management’s 2026 sales guidance (3%–4%) and then normalizes to mid/upper-2%s over 2027–2030.

EBIT margin improves gradually from the 2023–2025 trajectory, consistent with continued execution of transformation and productivity initiatives. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))

DCF cash flow durability is supported by depreciation and amortization intensity and recurring capex intensity, using historical averages as the initial forecast priors. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))

Working capital intensity is held near the historical average implied by balance sheet current assets/liabilities (excluding cash and short-term borrowings). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Macro/industry demand volatility affecting order cadence and pricing, especially in residential and pool-related end markets.
Material cost inflation/tariff and foreign exchange impacts compressing operating margin versus the base-case path.
Working capital and capex may deviate from historical intensity, reducing free cash flow conversion.

valuation_summary: Selected DCF drivers are derived directly from GAAP income statement and cash flow statement items in Pentair’s FY 2025 Form 10-K, reducing model input risk. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000007/pnr-20251231.htm))
Terminal value uses a Gordon-growth approach with conservative long-run growth and a moderate WACC assumption; scenarios adjust only a few key levers (growth, margins, WACC/terminal growth).
Comps are included for peer list completeness, but specific EV/NTM and P/E NTM inputs were not captured from a primary/high-quality market-data source within this run.
